attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Restates his comparison of the evidence, including 'in perpetuity'. Taking 'this' to mean generative AI fits the context. Calling it an observation about the evidence, not a forecast, is defensible.

contract.note: Reading 'proof' as credible evidence and 'real industry' as a commercially sustainable sector is an ordinary plain reading. The result still depends on an evidential threshold and a sector boundary the speaker never gave.

evidence.note: OpenAI's projected 2024 loss, available before the post. It covers one company and is an estimate, not sector-wide results or proof of permanent losses.
Turing says it was profitable in 2024. This is a company disclosure from one supplier that may serve loss-making labs, so it does not settle whether the sector is sustainable.

reviews.rationale: The packet has one company's loss projection and one supplier's self-reported profit. The contract needs a sector-wide accounting of costs and revenue as of 2025-02-24, and none was obtained. So the comparative claim about how strong the evidence was can neither be confirmed nor refuted.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words and his own calculation in his post.

semantics.note: Keeps 'without ChatGPT', 'it appears' and the 147M benchmark. 'It appears' presents a conclusion drawn from his data, not a probability hedge, so this is scored as an observation.

contract.note: Using January 2025 app MAU outside China, with DeepSeek included, follows the surrounding text. The tolerance for 'a little more than half' and the mismatch between the outside-China total and a worldwide benchmark are open interpretive choices.

evidence.note: The a16z ranking implies many more gen-AI apps had over 8M MAU, which casts doubt on his narrow app list. But it is global and mixes app categories, so it gives no matching total.
Secondary report of Superdata's estimate of 147M monthly users in May 2018. It does not confirm that this was the all-time peak.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no January 2025 total for gen-AI app MAU outside China. The a16z data raises doubts but is global and cannot be converted to the contract's measure. The benchmark is only partly documented. His own figures cannot verify themselves, so the evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Reading 'its' as OpenAI fits the context. The proposition keeps the comparison with traditional software and the compute-intensity cause, and correctly treats it as total cost rising with users.

contract.note: Requiring a materially heavier incremental cost than conventional software is the ordinary reading. Choosing Q4 2024 as the proxy period and leaving the comparator software unnamed are interpretive choices the speaker did not supply.

evidence.note: OpenAI says advanced capabilities need significantly more compute. This fits the proposed mechanism, but there is no cost-versus-users data and no comparison with other software.
Prompt caching reuses earlier computation, which limits simple linear scaling. Discounts to customers do not measure OpenAI's own serving costs.
Epoch models energy per query, without measured deployment data. It is not an operating-cost series and has no conventional-software comparison.

reviews.rationale: The packet suggests inference is compute-heavy but has no matched data on OpenAI's usage and serving costs, and no measured comparison with conventional software. The contract's requirements are not met, so the causal and comparative claim stays unsettled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The consequent 'will only go up' is firm and the antecedent is kept. The hedge 'it is unclear whether' applies only to the antecedent. 'Rise' slightly flattens 'only go up', and the contract flags this.

contract.note: Reading the claim as realized operating costs is literal and fair. A before-and-after comparison could credit increases driven by growth rather than Oracle pricing. This does not matter yet because the antecedent is unknown.

evidence.note: Company disclosure dated July 2025 confirming the Oracle capacity deal. It gives no effective prices, subsidy terms or realized costs.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent, that Oracle's terms are not like Microsoft's discounted ones, is unknown: no effective prices are established. No realized cost comparison exists, and the early-resolution rule is not met. With an open horizon and an unknown antecedent, the forecast cannot be scored.
